name: Toran Hill Resort Restaurant (GTDC)
why_it_matters: Gujarat Tourism Development Corporation's (GTDC) flagship Saputara property — the in-house restaurant serves unlimited Gujarati thali to resort guests and day-walk-ins. ₹160 thali; cleanest food-hygiene in Saputara per Tripadvisor reviews. Wins as the lunch stop for day-trippers from Surat/Vadodara who aren't staying overnight. Same thali every day; multi-day stayers describe it as 'monotonous' but the one-time hit is solid.
insider_tip: Lunch (12-3pm) is the right window — fresher than dinner. Walk-ins for thali only are permitted; no breakfast unless you're staying. Skip if you're here in monsoon (Jun-Sep); the resort drops to half-capacity and the kitchen runs leaner.
signature_address: Toran Hill Resort (GTDC), Near Pushpak Ropeway, Saputara, Dang District, Gujarat 394720

name: The Pasand Restaurant at Patang Residency
why_it_matters: Patang Residency is a 44-room Saputara Lake-shore hotel — The Pasand is the upper-floor restaurant with full lake-and-garden view, the Sun Café below is the casual sit-down. Multi-cuisine but the Indian section is the strongest. Won the Sunset-Point-side traveller crowd (1km from Sunset Point, 1km from Pushpak Ropeway). Tripadvisor mid-3 range.
insider_tip: Window seats face the lake — request specifically. Lunch is calmer; dinner buses-in tour groups. The veg sizzler is the menu's most ordered item. Avoid the continental section.
signature_address: Patang Residency, Saputara Lake Shore, Main Road, Saputara, Dang District, Gujarat 394720

name: Sunset Point Bhajiya Stalls (Monsoon)
signature_dish: Hot pakora and corn during monsoon
why_it_matters: Monsoon (July-September) is Saputara's peak season — Gujarat's only hill station gets 1,500-2,000mm of rain. The road to Sunset Point and around Lake Garden lights up with bhajiya/pakora carts catering to monsoon-festival visitors. Hot fried snacks + masala chai + lake-mist views is the Saputara monsoon experience that's been the same since the 1970s.
insider_tip: Active only July-September — outside monsoon, most carts are gone. Stalls run hottest 4pm-7pm to catch the Sunset Point crowd. Mirchi pakora (chilli fritter) is the local order; pyaaz (onion) is the safer one for kids. Carry cash; UPI works at maybe 1 in 5 carts.
signature_address: Sunset Point / Table Point Road, Saputara, Dang District, Gujarat 394720

name: Lake Garden Cafe (GTDC)
signature_dish: Snacks and tea by the lake
why_it_matters: GTDC-operated café on Saputara Lake's garden side, near the boating jetty. Convenient stop for visitors doing the lake-walk + boating + Sunset Point loop. Cafeteria-style ordering, no AC, lake-edge seating. Cleaner than the carts on Sunset Point road; pricier by ~30%.
insider_tip: Best as a mid-afternoon stop, not a destination meal. The samosa-chai pairing is the order most regulars get; avoid the dosa (the South Indian section is reheated batter). Lake-edge benches fill up between 3-6pm; arrive earlier for the view.
signature_address: Saputara Lake Garden, Near Boating Jetty, Saputara, Dang District, Gujarat 394720
